question.problem:
Find the shortest distance between the origin and the osculating plane for the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(1,-1,5)$ where $t=0,$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{14}}⟨-2,-1,3⟩,\,N(0)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨1,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the position vector of the point $P(1,-1,5)$ is $p=i-j+5\,k.$

We need to find a vector that's perpendicular to the osculating plane. To do that, we use the cross product of the unit tangent $T(0)$ and the principal normal $N(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =T(0)\times N(0) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{14}}⟨-2,-1,3⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨1,1,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{42}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{42}}[\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{42}}(-4\,i+5\,j-\,k)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the shortest distance between our plane and the origin is given by

$$
d=\frac{|(p-0)\cdot n|}{‖n‖}=\frac{|p\cdot n|}{‖n‖}=|p\cdot n|,
$$

since $‖n‖=1.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|p\cdot n| \\  & =|(i-j+5\,k)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{42}}(-4\,i+5\,j-\,k)| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{42}}|-4-5-5| \\  & =\frac{|-14|}{\sqrt{42}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{42}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
